title: Neighborhood score back-test: what predicted tract house-price growth relative to its own county
question: Within a county, did tracts that ranked higher on a signal at the start of a 5-year window see more house-price growth than the county's median tract over that window?

outcome.measure: ln(HPI end / HPI start) for the tract minus the county median of the same, FHFA annual tract HPI (developmental index, not seasonally adjusted)
outcome.tract_codes: 2020 Census tracts (63,015 of 63,743 FHFA tract codes in the 2019 rows match the 2020 Gazetteer; 46,532 match 2010)

sample.selection: largest 50 counties by block groups in counties/manifest.json, Connecticut excluded (2022 planning regions have no 2010 tract codes)
sample.tract_join: tract code present in both the 2010 and 2020 tract lists and land area changed by less than 5%
sample.bias_note: Tracts that were split or merged in 2020 (usually the fastest-growing ones) are excluded, and FHFA only publishes tracts with enough repeat sales, so new-build areas and thinly traded tracts are under-represented.

method.univariate: Spearman rank correlation per county, averaged over counties; Q5-Q1 = mean relative change of the top fifth of tracts by the signal minus the bottom fifth, averaged over counties; 90% intervals from 2000 bootstrap draws over counties (seeded).
method.composite: ridge regression (lambda 0.001) of the winsorised (1%/99%) relative outcome on within-county percentile ranks (centred), tested out of sample: on the other period, and on the other half of the counties in the other period.
method.supported_rule: a signal is supported if its mean Spearman has the same sign in both periods and the 90% interval excludes zero in both.

engine_model.fitted_on: P1 + P2 pooled, all sample counties
engine_model.note: Feature selection used both periods, so engine_model.out_of_sample_check is optimistic; out_of_sample.composite_bundle_fields (all bundle fields, no selection) is the honest figure.

headline: Cheaper-than-county tracts gained more: Spearman 0.713 (2015-20) and 0.183 (2020-25); top-vs-bottom-fifth gap 19.21% and 4.25% over 5 years.
Prior 5-year price momentum did not carry forward: Spearman -0.128 (2015-20) and 0.06 (2020-25).
A composite of every bundle field, fitted on 2015-20 and tested on 2020-25: Spearman 0.176 (90% 0.117 to 0.235), versus 0.183 for "cheapest tracts" alone.
No combination beat the cheapest-tracts baseline in every test, so the score is a relative-value screen, not a forecast.

sources.name: FHFA House Price Index, annual, census tracts (developmental index; not seasonally adjusted)
Census ACS 2015-2019 5-year, table-based prototype summary files
Census ACS 2010-2014 5-year, sequence summary files by state (tracts and block groups)

limitations: Tract level (bundles are block groups; the engine applies tract-tested relations to block-group values, many of which are tract medians anyway).
Two 5-year windows only (2015-2020, 2020-2025); the second contains the 2020-2022 boom.
Relative to county, not to the CBSA metro; a county-wide boom or bust is not predicted.
FHFA tract HPI is a developmental repeat-sales index; thin tracts are noisy, which biases correlations toward zero.
ACS 5-year medians are 5-year averages with sampling error; a tract median is not a block-group fact.
Says nothing about rents, cash flow, or what a specific improvement adds.
